items.q: A 24-year-old has several flat brown spots under 1 cm on the cheeks with no surface change. The correct morphologic term is?
items.exp: A macule is a flat circumscribed colour change under about 1 cm with no elevation or depression; larger flat lesions are patches.
r: Correct. Flat and small with only colour change.
Incorrect. A papule is elevated.
Incorrect. A plaque is elevated and broad.
Incorrect. A nodule is deep and palpable.

items.q: A raised flat-topped lesion over 1 cm on the elbow with scale is best termed?
items.exp: A plaque is an elevated flat-topped lesion broader than about 1 cm, often formed by coalescing papules as in psoriasis.
r: Correct. Broad, raised and flat-topped.
Incorrect. A vesicle holds clear fluid.
Incorrect. A pustule holds pus.
Incorrect. A papule is smaller than 1 cm.

items.q: A clear fluid-filled blister 3 mm on the lip versus a 1.5 cm one on the forearm differ as?
items.exp: Vesicles are fluid-filled blisters under about 0.5 cm; larger ones are bullae. Size, not cause, separates the terms.
r: Incorrect. Both are solid lesions.
Incorrect. Both are flat lesions.
Correct. Small is vesicle, large is bulla.
Incorrect. The order is reversed.
items.kp: Fluid plus size names the blister.

items.q: Lateral pressure on normal-looking skin near a blister extends the erosion. This Nikolsky sign is expected in?
items.exp: Nikolsky sign reflects intraepidermal acantholysis and is positive in pemphigus, staphylococcal scalded skin and toxic epidermal necrolysis.
r: Incorrect. A tender shin nodule, no epidermal split.
Correct. Suprabasal split shears with pressure.
Incorrect. Tense subepidermal blisters resist shear.
Incorrect. Intensely itchy papulovesicles, Nikolsky negative.

items.q: Gentle removal of scale from an elbow plaque produces pinpoint bleeding. This Auspitz sign points to?
items.exp: Auspitz sign is pinpoint bleeding after scale removal in psoriasis from thinned suprapapillary plates over dilated capillaries.
r: Incorrect. Wickham striae, not bleeding points.
Correct. Pinpoint bleed after grattage.
Incorrect. Collarette scale without Auspitz.
Incorrect. Greasy scale without Auspitz.
items.kp: Bleeding points under scale mean psoriasis.

items.q: New linear papules appear along a scratch mark in a patient with flat-topped violaceous papules. This Koebner phenomenon also occurs in?
items.exp: Koebnerisation is new lesions of the same disease at trauma sites, classic in psoriasis, lichen planus and vitiligo.
r: Incorrect. Infections spread by contact, not Koebner.
Incorrect. These do not koebnerise.
Incorrect. Pigmentary, not traumatic.
Correct. Psoriasis and vitiligo koebnerise.
items.kp: Trauma planting same lesions is Koebner.

items.q: Under Wood lamp a vitiligo patch shows bright blue-white fluorescence while surrounding skin stays dull. The lamp wavelength used is?
items.exp: Wood lamp emits long-wave UVA near 365 nm in a dark room, accentuating depigmentation and some pigment or infections by fluorescence.
r: Incorrect. Infrared gives no fluorescence.
Incorrect. Plain visible light adds nothing.
Correct. UVA near 365 nm.
Incorrect. Short-wave UVC burns and is not used.

items.q: Skin scrapings from an annular itchy ring lesion mounted in potassium hydroxide show branching septate hyphae. This confirms?
items.exp: KOH dissolves keratin leaving fungal hyphae visible; branching septate hyphae indicate dermatophyte tinea.
r: Incorrect. Mites need mineral-oil mount.
Correct. Septate branching hyphae are dermatophytes.
Incorrect. Candida shows pseudohyphae with budding yeast.
Incorrect. Bacteria need Gram stain or culture.
items.kp: Septate branches in KOH mean tinea.

items.q: A Tzanck smear from the base of grouped genital vesicles shows multinucleated giant cells. The most likely cause is?
items.exp: Multinucleated giant cells on Tzanck smear indicate herpesvirus cytopathic effect, seen in herpes simplex and zoster.
r: Correct. Ballooning multinucleated giants are herpetic.
Incorrect. That shows single acantholytic cells.
Incorrect. That shows neutrophils and cocci.
Incorrect. That shows no diagnostic cells.

items.q: For a new tense blister suspected to be bullous pemphigoid, the best biopsy plan is?
o: Shave of the blister roof only
Excision of the whole blister with surrounding fat
Curettage of the blister base only
Punch at the blister edge for histology plus perilesional skin for direct immunofluorescence
items.exp: Edge punch captures the split level for histology while perilesional skin preserves immune deposits for direct immunofluorescence.
r: Incorrect. Roof alone loses the split level.
Incorrect. Excision is excessive for diagnosis.
Incorrect. Base alone misses the roof and deposits.
Correct. Edge plus perilesional DIF is the standard pair.
items.kp: Edge for level plus perilesional for DIF.
